# mindfork

> A terminal AI chat written in Rust: local models via llama.cpp or OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Grok in the cloud — with persistent memory, notes, RAG and tools. Windows and Linux.

Run local models through llama.cpp — or bring OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Grok. Persistent memory, notes and RAG, an agentic tool loop that reaches your own code project: one fast native binary for Windows and Linux.

## Start here

- [Install](https://mindfork.io/install/): Download mindfork for Windows or Linux: the installer, the packages, the portable archives — what each one is for, how to verify it, and what to do first.
- [Source on GitHub](https://github.com/vshylov/mindfork-rs): the source, the issue tracker and the releases

## Articles

- [mindfork at a glance](https://mindfork.io/articles/mindfork-at-a-glance/): The shape of the app: an engine contract over OpenAI-compatible servers, a client-side agentic loop, one turn from start to finish, layered memory, boring durable storage — and where the trust boundaries are.
- [Why the engine is a server, not a library](https://mindfork.io/articles/engine-as-a-server/): mindfork nearly embedded an inference runtime. The contract that replaced it made a local GGUF and a cloud frontier model the same thing.
- [The self-model: a memory that knows it changed](https://mindfork.io/articles/self-model/): Each companion keeps a model of itself and of you — a summary, goals, traits and dated observations — and maintains it with its own tools, on your disk.
- [Where vector search earns its keep](https://mindfork.io/articles/vector-search/): One small embedding server powers the knowledge base, large attachments, notes and memory — and the app notices when you swap the model under it.
- [The same answer, sooner](https://mindfork.io/articles/local-speed/): FlashAttention and speculative decoding in managed mode: two llama.cpp levers that change how fast tokens arrive — without trading away the answer.
- [Why the Python sandbox is WebAssembly, not Docker](https://mindfork.io/articles/python-sandbox/): python_exec runs model-written code in a CPython compiled to WebAssembly — numpy, pandas and requests included — inside a box that ships with the app and, by default, cannot see your machine.
- [Where the trust boundaries are](https://mindfork.io/articles/trust-boundaries/): An assistant that can browse, run code and edit your project needs edges, not promises: what leaves the machine, where the model may not point, what the code can touch, when the app asks — and what the author receives, which is nothing.
- [The code workspace: containment before capability](https://mindfork.io/articles/code-workspace/): A project attached to a chat: what the assistant can read, edit and run there, why the commands are only ever yours, how every change is a diff with a way back — and the semantic index that was measured and did not ship.
- [Background runs, and the pool they share](https://mindfork.io/articles/background-runs/): A subagent that outlives its round, the app's own quiet requests, and one local llama-server with one context pool under all of them: what the server does when the pool overflows, how the app keeps it from happening, and what parallel sessions actually buy on one GPU.

## News

- [mindfork 0.11.2 — a bigger model on a smaller card, and a long page read whole](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-11-2/): The managed llama.cpp server takes the arguments the settings have no field for, so a 26B mixture-of-experts model fits in 8.4 GB of video memory instead of 17.3. And a page the assistant fetches arrives whole up to a million characters and can be searched in the same reply — the last chapter of an 81-page specification, found with one search.
- [mindfork 0.11.1 — the install script works on a rented pod](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-11-1/): 0.11.0's one-line install failed on RunPod before it had unpacked a single file. The first real run found it; this release carries the fix, the test that reproduces the pod's shape, and the result that the rest of the line — llama.cpp with CUDA, the sandbox, a 31B model verified at a 131k context — ran on that pod as designed.
- [mindfork 0.11.0 — from a bare Linux machine to a local model, in one line](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-11-0/): A new command installs the Python sandbox and llama.cpp and writes the model, its projector, the embedding model and the context into the settings — checked before anything is downloaded, and started once to prove it loads. An install script puts the app on the machine first. Written for a rented GPU box that is new at every stop; just as good on a desktop. And llama setup installs CUDA builds on Linux, which it had been refusing.
- [mindfork 0.10.2 — which copy of your data is the newest](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-10-2/): One command says when each copy of your data was last written and what it holds — the data on this computer or a backup archive, without restoring anything — and a second says what each copy has that the other lacks. And opening a chat no longer flashes the one you were leaving.
- [mindfork is public](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-is-public/): The repository is open, the first public release is out, and this is what the project is — an AI chat that lives in your terminal, with memory that persists and tools that stay behind switches you set.
- [mindfork 0.9.9 — files in, charts out, work in the background](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-9-9/): The assistant's Python code reads the chat's files and hands back what it saves. Subagents and staged dialogues run in the background while you keep talking, with a screen to watch them. The engine downloads itself — and the web tools wait for your say-so.
- [mindfork 0.9.8 — give it real work](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-9-8/): A code project attached to a chat — read, edit, build and test, every change reviewable and revertible. Subagents with real tools and live transcripts. And web search that can stop being rate-limited.
- [mindfork 0.9.7 — wherever your terminal is](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-9-7/): Every action has a typed command, copying works over SSH, a conversation exports to a file — and the assistant can find what you said in another chat.
- [mindfork 0.9.6 — the model can see](https://mindfork.io/blog/mindfork-0-9-6/): Images in a message from a file, the clipboard or a URL; tool screenshots reach the model; the web tools stop at your front door; a cloud blip no longer costs the turn.
- [Hello from mindfork 0.9.5](https://mindfork.io/blog/hello-mindfork/): The project gets a home on the web — and a status report: an interactive demo, a fourth cloud provider, history compression.

## Optional

- [Privacy policy](https://mindfork.io/privacy/): What mindfork keeps on your machine, what leaves it and only on which setting of yours, and what reaches its author — which is nothing.
- [Disclaimer](https://mindfork.io/disclaimer/): The app ships no model: what that means for the output you get, for the tools a model may invoke on your machine, and for warranty and liability.
